item.description: EUGENE, OREGON - NOVEMBER 14: Head Coach Kyle Whittingham of the Michigan Wolverines runs off the field at halftime during the game against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Eugene, Oregon. Changes needed to be made, and Harbaugh made many. “Do it or die trying” was Harbaugh’s mantra about beating Ohio State and all of Michigan’s opponents. Another huge change Harbaugh made was changing the 9-on-7 practice period. “It means everything to us; we got the music going, we got the energy going,” former Michigan linebacker Josh Ross said in 2021 . “It’s exciting; we do it every single week.” “We’re blasting music, smelling salts, everything. item.title: 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List No. 12
item.description: PHOENIX, AZ - JUNE 24: Carson Bolemon #18 poses for a photo during the 2026 Draft Combine at Arizona Grand Resort Phoenix on Wednesday, June 24, 2026 in Phoenix, Arizona. (Photo by Aryanna Frank/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images We’re a quarter of the way through the 2027 Willie McCovey Memorial Community Prospect List! Our goal is to rank the top 44 prospects in the San Francisco Giants organization, and we’ve officially hit the 25% mark! Rounding out the first quarter is one of the many new players to the system who is on the list: left-handed pitcher Carson Bolemon, who makes his CPL debut as the No. 11 prospect in the system. The Giants drafted Bolemon with the 29th pick in July’s draft out of Southside Christian School in South Carolina. While he’s a little old for a prep player (he’ll turn 20 in April), he’s extremely experienced, as he not only starred in high school (where he threw a 19-strikeout no-hitter in the state championship game), but was also the ace of the 18-and-under Team USA squad that won the World Cup in 2025. Depending on how you like to view things, it’s either good or bad news that Bolemon was available to the Giants at No. 29, since he entered the season as the consensus top pitcher in the draft. Seen through an optimistic lens, the Giants were able to capitalize on a mildly-down year and get the pre-season top-ranked pitcher … as well as the post-season top-ranked pitcher, Jackson Flora. Seen through a more pessimistic lens, the Giants drafted a player who has already started moving downwards, as he was the ninth pitcher off the board in July, after being projected to be the first pitcher off the board a year ago. Bolemon, who is a well-built 6’4, and who famously didn’t give up a single earned run his junior year, has a fastball that’s been a little inconsistent in terms of velocity, but that has good movement that should allow it to play against righties and lefties alike. He has a very intriguing curveball, while also throwing a changeup and a sweeper, and scouts have raved about his makeup. The Giants were able to draft Bolemon because they acquired the competitive balance-round pick from the Cleveland Guardians in the Patrick Bailey trade, and ultimately those two will forever be linked. That trade will remain something of a “TBD” until we learn how good Bolemon can be, and we’re still many years away from that. Until then, we can look forward to seeing the youngster on the mound in 2027 for his professional debut, as he didn’t pitch (other than in unofficial games) post-draft. It will be interesting to see whether the Giants have Bolemon begin the year in the Arizona Complex League, or if they get him out at the start of the season by sending him to Low-A San Jose. item.title: BYU has never won a Maui Invitational championship. How can this year’s Cougars change that?
item.description: BYU players prepare to take the court against Ohio State on Nov. 2, 2026, at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City. | BYU Photo LAHAINA, Hawaii — The Lahaina Civic Center gymnasium is packed with history. Banners hang from its rafters commemorating past Maui Invitational champions, with Duke, North Carolina and Kansas dominating the count. Walls of the arena are dedicated to former Maui standouts and tournament MVPs, such as Kemba Walker, Adam Morrison, Bobby Hurley and Penny Hardaway. Nowhere to be found in the historic gym, however, is a lasting trace of BYU, despite the Cougars having participated in the Maui Invitational there four times before. In fact, as BYU makes its fifth-ever Maui appearance this week, the Cougars are now tied with San Diego State for the second-most times playing in the event without capturing a championship there. Only Memphis has made more trips to Maui (six) without ever hoisting the Wayne Duke trophy, which is presented to the lone unbeaten team after three days of hoops. Additionally, BYU has never produced an invitational MVP, and only one former Cougar — Tyler Haws in 2014 — has landed on the All-Tournament team. Given the current state of both November multi-team events and college basketball as a whole, perhaps 2026 will be the last time BYU graces the Civic Center hardwood in Lahaina and drains shots on the arena’s famous “soft rims.” It’s a shame that one of the sport’s most unique and prestigious early-season traditions is viewed as “on life support” and facing “an uncertain future.” The Protect College Sports Act could easily receive increased support from every political side if it included provisions to save the Maui Invitational — but that’s a thought for another day. If this week truly is the Cougars’ last dance in Maui, it’s their last chance to be crowned champions of the event. And it may be the best such chance they’ve ever had to do so. BYU (No. 25 in KenPom) opens its Maui slate Monday against Washington (No. 88), then will face either Ole Miss (No. 27) or Clemson (No. 75) on Tuesday. Two wins would put the Cougars in Wednesday’s title game, where many fans and pundits anticipate them to meet fellow Big 12 foe Arizona, assuming the Wildcats can survive their bracket of Colorado State, Providence and VCU. Not since 1992 has BYU reached the Maui championship game. The Cougars will likely be favored on both Monday and Tuesday, and in a situation with three games in three days, anything can happen in that third game — even toppling Arizona, if need be. “A lot of it’s going to come down to just toughness,” BYU head coach Kevin Young said of the invitational’s rapid-fire format. “I think our guys possess a lot of that.” BYU’s first time in Maui, 1992, saw the Cougars finish as runners-up, beating No. 9 Oklahoma and then Penny Hardaway-led Memphis before falling to Grant Hill, Bobby Hurley and No. 1 Duke in the championship. item.description: ANAHEIM, CALIFORNIA - JULY 19: Matt Vierling #8 of the Detroit Tigers at bat during the game against the Los Angeles Angels at Angel Stadium of Anaheim on July 19, 2026 in Anaheim, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The deadline to tender contracts to arbitration eligible players has come and gone, meaning the free agent market has once again been flooded with prospective players. Usually, there are some surprises included in that batch, but for the most part, stock held true. The Phillies were included in this group, sending out offers to players that should help them in 2027 while pruning the extra roster spots for future use. This new crop of players from which the Phillies can sift through does have some interesting names that match some of the needs the team has. Them not getting a contract offer means that some of the warts they possess were too much to spend money on, but there can still be a bargain or two if looking hard enough. It’s not the greatest of players to choose from, but hey – you never know! Let’s look at some of those players the Phillies could have an interest in this offseason. Davis Schneider – If finding a player that can play multiple positions defensively while also batting from the right side is a goal of the offseason, signing Schneider is an option. There’s just one little bitty problem: Schneider kind of stinks. He’s played left field and second base in 2026, third base a few times in 2025….and hit like a backup catcher. He doesn’t chase that much, which is a nice skill to have, but so is actually making contact with the ball. He showed flashes of what he could do in 2025 when he posted a 118 OPS+ by hitting for some pop and showing a good amount of patience, but he fell back to Earth in 2026, hitting a paltry .145/.310/.315 (77 OPS+). Bringing him onto the roster would at least bolster the bench a bit, but this one feels like a player that could be had on a minor league deal. Probably don’t want to guarantee much of anything. item.title: Josh Jacobs not expected to play vs Rams
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams could be catching a break against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Green Bay is not expecting running back Josh Jacobs to play as he continues recovering from surgery to repair a fractured right ring finger. His expected absence could further complicate an already struggling Packers rushing attack and give the Rams’ defense another reason to anticipate a pass-heavy offensive approach. Josh Jacobs, with his surgically repaired right ring finger heavily protected, is giving it a go even though coach Matt LaFleur said he didn’t think it was very likely that Jacobs could play on Wednesday. Jacobs would need to convince them he could hold onto the football for… pic.twitter.com/LYcXBBV50p — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) November 21, 2026 Jacobs suffered the injury during Green Bay’s Week 9 victory over the New England Patriots and underwent surgery on November 13. Although he has returned to individual work, head coach Matt LaFleur indicated that Jacobs remains unlikely to suit up against Los Angeles. He will need to demonstrate that he can properly handle the football before returning to game action. It has been an incredibly up-and-down season for Jacobs. He missed the first six games while on the Commissioner’s Exempt List following off-field legal issues before returning in Week 7. Unfortunately, his return has not gone as planned. Across three appearances, Jacobs has recorded just 80 rushing yards on 36 carries, averaging a career-low 2.2 yards per attempt. Green Bay has struggled to establish consistency on the ground throughout the season. Through its first eight games, the Packers averaged just 60.6 rushing yards per game, one of the worst marks in the NFL. Even with Jacobs sidelined, the backfield has struggled to provide a dependable alternative. Without Jacobs, the Rams can enter Wednesday’s matchup with a clearer expectation of what Green Bay wants to do offensively. While Kaleb Johnson and the other available running backs will still get opportunities, Los Angeles can focus more attention on slowing down the passing game. That doesn’t mean the Packers will abandon the run entirely, but the Rams should have fewer reasons to fear a consistent ground attack. With the opportunity to make Green Bay one-dimensional, Los Angeles’ pass rush and secondary could play a significant role in determining the outcome.

item.title: Adrian Morejon rejects QO, who emerges as Padres LH relief options
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers LH reliever Alex Vesia could be a potential free-agent signing. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images As expected, Adrian Morejon rejected the San Diego Padres’ one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer. While the Friar Faithful were disappointed by his decision, the door has not closed on Morejon returning to San Diego. However, the Padres cannot afford to wait and risk losing an opportunity to sign a top free-agent left-handed reliever. The free-agent market offers multiple candidates who have a proven track record of recording outs in late-inning pressure situations. Implications from Morejon’s decision The thought of Morejon not wearing the Brown & Gold is disappointing but feels inevitable. He is one of the premier free agent pitchers available, and multiple suitors will aggressively vie for him. After all, what franchise isn’t in the market for a hard-throwing left-handed reliever? Suddenly, bullpen reconstruction will become a priority if Morejon leaves town. Friars President of Baseball Operations & General Manager A.J. Preller will be forced to add another bullpen arm alongside the game’s top closer, Mason Miller. Guaranteed, he has already identified several lefty targets if his worst nightmare becomes reality. Other teams are chasing the same needs; the Padres must bid aggressively on their top targets or risk getting left behind. Filling the void: Morejon’s replacement options Replacing Morejon is a slightly different task than searching for a lefty specialist. The Padres need to sign a left-handed reliever who can handle a similar workload. Morejon has appeared in 151 games over the last two seasons. The Friars already have plenty of left-handed bullpen depth, led by Kyle Hart, Yuki Matsui, and Wandy Peralta. However, each is brought in to face one or two left-handed hitters and end a potential scoring threat. The Padres will enter the market and look to add a proven left-handed setup reliever who can pitch multiple innings. Their eyes should be on Los Angeles Dodgers left-hander Alex Vesia, who has success as a setup reliever. He is the ideal replacement for Morejon; his mound presence ensures the bullpen retains last season’s dominant edge. He cannot match Morejon’s velocity, but Vesia averaged 11.5 strikeouts per nine innings, well above last season’s major league average. He misses bats and induces opposing batters to hit into double plays with his vertical dropping four-seam fastball. Chicago White Sox Sean Newcomb is the next best free-agent option. item.title: Fernando Mendoza shows his mettle as Broncos gallop past Raiders 38-24
item.description: (Photo by Justin Tafoya/Getty Images) | Getty Images What looked like a runaway division win by the Denver Broncos instead turned into Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback showcasing his mettle on a brisk Mile High Sunday afternoon. Facing yet another stingy defense, the Silver & Black’s prized No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft had his moments of inaccuracy and panic — as expected from a rookie quarterback — but the Indiana product showed off his arm talent, mental toughness, and poise that made Mendoza worthy of the top overall selection, despite a tough 38-24 division defeat. At the forefront of the Raiders offense, Mendoza helped orchestrate a trio of touchdown drives, much to the chagrin of Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph. Las Vegas franchise quarterback’s first official touchdown was a beauty of a loft to running back Ashton Jeanty who torched Denver outside linebacker Que Robinson on a wheel route for a 68-yard catch-and-run, to trim the disadvantage to 17-10 before halftime. And in the third quarter, Mendoza displayed a filthy handoff fake that froze elite cornerback Pat Surtain II and allowed veteran tight end Ian Thomas to slither past for a 19-yard touchdown to tie the ball game at 17 apiece. Make that TWO TDs for Fernando Mendoza 🗣️ LVvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sgnbFG3sUr — NFL (@NFL) November 22, 2026 Even after Denver sprinted ahead with back-to-back touchdown drives after Las Vegas tied the contest to take a 31-17 lead, Mendoza didn’t wilt — even with the Raiders in obvious passing mode trying to catch up. The 6-foot-5 and 225-pound quarterback went 7-for-7 during an eight-play, 69-yard scoring drive that showed the variety of throws Mendoza can make. From short strikes to a long ball (39-yard dime to fleet-footed wide receiver Tre Tucker), the 23-year-old spread the ball around before finding wideout Jack Bech for a seven-yard touchdown pass. item.title: Syracuse men’s basketball: fans don’t have to pretend all wins are good ones
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Syracuse, New York, USA; Syracuse Orange head coach Gerry McNamara reacts during the second half against the Lafayette Leopards at the JMA Wireless Dome. Mandatory Credit: Rich Barnes-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After watching the Syracuse Orange struggle with Cornell on Wednesday, I assumed that Saturday’s game would bring out a focused, energetic squad. That didn’t happen and after having to pull out all the stops to win 84-81 over a Lafayette team that had lost by 36 to Butler and 28 to St. Bonaventure, Gerry McNamara was asked a question about the margin of victory in the wins this week. “I don’t worry. I’ll let other people worry about that nonsense, bullshit, I don’t care. Win a game you know. That’s how I grew up…..I’m not going to worry about margin of victory, all that. I know the next game I play I’m going to coach to win again. So I don’t worry about al the other stuff because at the end of the day you’re still going to have those opponents to play anyway so if you beat them, the margin of victory doesn’t, just win the game you’re playing in front of you. So my focus is on can we continue to get better.” McNamara ended the answer by talking about shooting and offense, but is that the issue? Can we talk about Syracuse’s defense giving up 80+ points to two teams this week? What about the fact that Cornell and Lafayette went 24-54 from 3 in the two games? Unfortunately for anyone who wants to espouse “Just win baby”, it’s not the case in today’s college basketball. Syracuse built their schedule around the NET formula and margin of victory against teams ranked 200th and 303rd in this morning’s KenPom is a factor. Winning 20 or 21 games might not be enough for an invite when the ACC is not off to a strong start. Right now Syracuse sits 81st in KenPom. Last year’s sub-500 team finished the year ranked 87th and the lowest ranked NCAA at-large team was Missouri who was 54th. Yes, it’s early. Yes, you have to win the games, but you cannot pretend that this shouldn’t be a concern….because it is. He went on to talk about not having juice, but why wait until it’s 20+ minutes in the game to make an adjustment to the press? This is still a young staff and they sure don’t seem to have a grasp on what they want this team to be this season. If you’re heading into desperation mode against Lafayette, even with two starters injured, that’s a big warning sign. This was a November game that almost turned into a unfathomable loss and it wasn’t the time to lecture anyone about playing to win the game. I’m sensititve to the fact that Gerry’s dealing with a lot right now- on and off the court. I’m worried that the pressure he’s putting on himself to get this program back is too much, but you can’t get this agitated over a legitimate question. He didn’t mention ISIS , but there were a lot of Shafer vibes coming out of this one….let’s hope the Albany post-game talk stays out of “cutting people’s heads off” talk.

item.description: Freeman has 11 tries in 31 matches for England [Getty Images] England wing Tommy Freeman is in contention for Saturday's Nations Championship play-off meeting with New Zealand. The 25-year-old has been a key part of England's backline this year, starting nine Tests in a row for before being rotated out of the side for their comprehensive win over Japan on 14 November. He was due to return for the 37-12 win over the All Blacks on Saturday, but a thigh issue forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off. Harlequins' Cadan Murley was called into the side to replace Freeman and impressed in an emphatic England performance. Head coach Steve Borthwick has bolstered his back-three options, which also include Gloucester's Will Joseph, by calling up Saracens' 20-year-old Noah Caluori. Caluori, who finished as joint-top try scorer in last year's Prem alongside Freeman, crossed on his England debut against Fiji in July and was a late replacement in the win over Argentina a week later. He also scored two tries in a England A's win over an Argentine equivalent earlier this month. Fly-half Fin Smith, who came off 55 minutes into the win over the All Blacks with cramp, is also in a 37-strong squad who have gathered at England's training base to prepare for Saturday's third-place play-off. England finished a point short of France in the northern hemisphere standings of the new format, missing out on a place in Sunday's Nations Championship final against South Africa. The result of England and New Zealand's meeting, along with the weekend's other five matches at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, will contribute to a Ryder Cup-style points race for the inaugural hemisphere shield. item.title: James Gallagher’s MMA career was so much more than the Ricky Bandejas loss
item.description: James Gallagher bidding farewell to mixed martial arts at age 30 on Sunday flooded my mind with memories of him as a teenage prodigy, bustling Bellator Dublin shows and a feeling that despite never realizing the glory he thought he would, his career is one of the most successful in Irish MMA history. A highlight reel of Ricky Bandejas’ 2018 upset of Gallagher will flicker through a lot of people’s minds when they think of “The Strabanimal.” There was a collective euphoria across social media back then seeing the 21-year-old eat a side kick before getting pounded out, just a few minutes after being all up in Bandejas’s face. It’s the quintessential “chat s***, get banged” scenario playing out at a live sporting event. In fact, it’s such a classic of the genre, you’ll likely still see it pop up on your feed today, nearly a decade later. To simmer Gallagher’s career down to that one brutal defeat would be massively underselling the impact he had on the sport in his home country, though. As a teenager, Gallagher was like a mythological creature. Fighting grown men at age 13, it wasn’t until he was introduced to SBG head coach John Kavanagh that his dream began to take shape. His jiu-jitsu ability was the first thing most people heard about him. Experienced black belts would wax lyrical about his potential after his move to Dublin. Then, after blitzing through all the youth competitions, he began showing up at adult events and proving it wasn’t just hot air. James Gallagher and coach John Kavanaugh were a formidable duo early in Gallagher's MMA run. ASSOCIATED PRESS There was a buzz across the mats when Gallagher was competing. Early on he’d sport an oversized judo gi borrowed from a teammate and it looked like you could’ve fit three of him in there if it wasn’t for the blue belt keeping the outfit together. He’d smile, shake your hand, and more often than not he’d be on your back, using that same hand to apply a rear-naked choke a few seconds later. Eventually, Gallagher turned his focus to MMA. item.title: Nationals reliever Erik Tolman given the Tony Conigliaro award for his inspirational rise
item.description: WASHINGTON, DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA - SEPTEMBER 27, 2026: Erik Tolman #73 of the Washington Nationals pitches during the ninth inning of a game against the New York Mets at Nationals Park on September 27, 2026 in Washington, District of Columbia. The Nationals beat the Mets, 6-4. (Photo by Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Erik Tolman’s debut and success in the big leagues was one of the best stories in baseball during the 2026 season. The Nats left handed reliever had to overcome so many obstacles to get on to an MLB mound, but he did it. Today, Tolman was awarded with the Tony Conigliaro Award, which is given to a big leaguer who has overcome adversity. honoring erik 🙌 the Tony Conigliaro Award award recognizes a major leaguer who has overcome adversity through the attributes of spirit, determination, and courage. pic.twitter.com/uHrAbbMGzM — Washington Nationals (@Nationals) November 23, 2026 Conigliaro was a Red Sox player in the late 1960’s who was on the road to superstardom before getting hit in the face with a ball. That hit by pitch caused major damage, including some vision loss. Despite that, Conigliaro came back after missing a season. He put up quality numbers in 1969 and 1970, before the vision problems became so bad, he could not play anymore. The award has been handed out since 1990, and is usually given out to players who dealt with serious injuries or other health issues. Wilson Ramos is the only other National to win the award. He won it in 2014 due to coming back from injuries and a kidnapping. Tolman now joins him as a Nat to win the award. Tolman’s story is a ridiculous tale of perseverance. He had to undergo Tommy John twice in a short period of time after being drafted. That is bad enough, but these days that is not unheard of. However, in his return, Tolman tore up every ligament in his knee and more after his foot got stuck jumping over the foul line. This clip from Just Baseball does a good job explaining everything. MLB’s Story of the YEAR Erik Tolman of the Nationals comeback story is incredible pic.twitter.com/ee8hI3rVrZ — Just Baseball (@JustBB_Media) November 6, 2026 The biggest long term health problem from that injury was foot drop. Tolman is unable to move his foot side to side due to nerve damage. During that injury, his peroneal nerve was cut. So when Tolman is on the mound, he has to wear an ankle brace for stabilization. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
